items.title: Provincial Deadline Pushes Mississauga to Finalize Heritage Status for Two Century-Old Buildings
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, city staff are recommending council designate two historic properties, a 1917 bungalow at 1 Godfrey's Lane in Port Credit and a 1908 building at 20 Thomas St. in Streetsville, as heritage sites despite objections from their owners. The outlet reports the recommendation goes before the city's general committee on Nov. 18 and stems from a provincial rule requiring heritage designation within two years of listing, or the city loses the ability to re-list a property for five years. Both buildings are already on the heritage registry, which only requires a 60 day demolition notice rather than full protection, mississauga.com reported. The bungalow's owners first objected in February 2024, leading council to defer its decision that September. The outlet notes the city has until Jan. 1, 2027 to act, and the documents provided disclose no redevelopment plans.

items.title: Months-Long Investigation Into Bolton Shooting Leads to New Firearm Charges for Two Mississauga Men
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Caledon OPP have laid additional firearm charges against two Mississauga men after a monthslong investigation into a shooting at a Bolton home earlier this year. The outlet reports officers were called after reports of gunfire, and while no injuries were reported, a suspect vehicle described as a white Kia SUV was seen leaving the area. Police say the probe led them to execute two search warrants at a Mississauga residence on April 21 and May 28, seizing roughly six grams of cocaine along with items connected to drug trafficking. Charges were first laid in June, including unauthorized possession of a prohibited firearm, insauga.com reported. In the latest update, Pragash Segatheesan, 36, of Mississauga, was charged on Oct. 22 with trafficking in a firearm, according to the outlet.

items.title: Ontario Announces Tripled Noise Fines for Loud Cars at Mississauga Press Event
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Ontario's transportation minister stood outside Peel Regional Police headquarters in Mississauga to announce the province intends to raise the minimum fine for excessively loud vehicles from $60 to $200. The outlet reports Minister Sarkaria said extreme noise disrupts communities and distracts drivers, adding that families should not have to put up with the noise outside their homes at any hour. Mississauga Mayor Alvin Tedjo, sworn in just days earlier as the city's eighth mayor, said the noise from cars racing on city streets is a quality of life issue that frustrates residents daily, according to insauga.com. The outlet also reports a regional official echoed those concerns, saying reckless driving has threatened the peace of neighbourhoods across the region. Insauga.com notes the announcement comes as Peel municipalities push for tougher enforcement.

items.title: Mississauga's Startup Ecosystem Backs Two FinTech Founders Targeting Slow International Payments
items.summary: According to BetaKit, two Mississauga based FinTech founders are tackling the slow, costly infrastructure behind international money transfers from different angles. The outlet reports Kavodax founder Gharsa Amin is using blockchain to speed up transfers, while Zpayd founder Gezim Ramabaja is building connections that let financial institutions offer bill payments globally. Amin told BetaKit the idea took shape after her grandmother fell ill in Germany and a transfer from Canada took five days and cost roughly three to four percent in exchange fees, forcing her grandmother to visit a bank in person for the funds. Amin, who had worked in digital banking, said she knew there had to be a better way and founded Kavodax in 2025 to cut the cost of overseas payments for small businesses. According to BetaKit, both founders have relied on Mississauga's startup ecosystem for mentorship.

items.title: PAI Brings Its First Menu Items Launched Outside Toronto to New Square One Location
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Toronto based Thai restaurant PAI will open its first location outside the city at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga on Dec. 15. The outlet reports PAI, founded by chef Nuit Regular and Jeff Regular in 2014, has built a reputation as one of Toronto's best Thai restaurants. Alongside its established favourites, the Square One location will be the first to serve new dishes, including a grilled fish platter called Miang Pla and a Yum Yai salad, before they reach other PAI locations next year, according to insauga.com. Chef Nuit Regular said the team has been looking forward to opening in Mississauga and introducing dishes for the first time alongside guest favourites. The outlet notes the location will also pay tribute to PAI's origins at The Curry Shack, the first restaurant the couple opened in Thailand.

items.title: Credit Valley Road Area Is Focus of Peel Police Search for Missing Mississauga Woman
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Peel Regional Police are searching for a 52 year old woman named Paula who was last seen on foot near Eglinton Avenue and Credit Valley Road in Mississauga on Nov. 17. The outlet reports Paula, whose surname was not released, is described as five feet five inches tall with a medium build, short black hair and brown eyes. Police said she was last seen wearing a grey T-shirt, black jogging pants and black running shoes. Mississauga.com reports officers are asking anyone with information on Paula's whereabouts to contact Peel police. The outlet notes few other details about the circumstances of her disappearance have been released publicly, and police have not said how long she had been missing before the bulletin was issued.

items.title: #NoGoodWay Day Campaign Turns Mississauga's Clock Tower Yellow to Retire the R-word
items.summary: According to motionball for Special Olympics, Mississauga's clock tower and city hall will be illuminated yellow on Nov. 18 to mark the national #NoGoodWay Day campaign. The organization says the campaign, running Nov. 4 to Nov. 18, aims to promote inclusive language for people with intellectual disabilities and end the casual use of the R-word. Motionball co-founder Paul Etherington said in a press release that Canadians can use their voices to challenge stereotypes and help build communities where people with intellectual disabilities are treated with respect and dignity. The organization is asking participants to wear yellow, sign an online pledge for inclusive language, and share videos of themselves symbolically destroying the R-word by tearing, deleting or erasing it. Mississauga joins other cities lighting landmarks yellow for the campaign, according to motionball.

items.title: Montcrest Becomes Second Company to Challenge Mississauga's Data Centre Moratorium at Tribunal
items.summary: According to Global News, Mississauga's one year ban on data centre construction is facing a second challenge at the Ontario Land Tribunal, this time from Toronto based real estate investment firm Montcrest Asset Management. The outlet reports Montcrest wants to build a data centre near Eglinton Avenue East and Tahoe Boulevard and is asking the tribunal to exempt its project from the moratorium. This comes as Prologis, an American warehouse developer, is separately challenging the same ban with the tribunal, according to Global News. Mississauga became one of the first Canadian cities to approve a one year data centre moratorium, which took effect in September after a unanimous council vote led in part by councillor turned mayor Alvin Tedjo. Tedjo said ahead of the vote that there were concerns about power consumption, heat islands and noise, Global News reported.
